issues.title: JEI compatibility mixin warnings when JEI is not installed (Fabric 26.3)
issues.body:
While testing AppleSkin on Minecraft 26.3 with Fabric and appleskin-fabric-mc26.3-3.0.10.jar, I noticed the following warnings during startup when JEI was not installed:

[main/WARN]: Error loading class: mezz/jei/fabric/platform/RenderHelper (java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: mezz/jei/fabric/platform/RenderHelper)
[main/WARN]: @Mixin target mezz.jei.fabric.platform.RenderHelper was not found appleskin.jei.mixins.json:JEIRenderHelperMixin from mod appleskin

After installing JEI on the same profile, both warnings disappeared.

AppleSkin appears to be attempting to resolve its JEI compatibility mixin even when JEI is absent.

This does not appear to cause any gameplay issues, but I wanted to report the unnecessary startup warnings.

issues.title: Use `HudElementRegistry` on Fabric rather than mixins
issues.body:
Fabric's [`HudElementRegistry`](https://maven.fabricmc.net/docs/fabric-api-0.155.2+26.1.2/net/fabricmc/fabric/api/client/rendering/v1/hud/HudElementRegistry.html) and [`VanillaHudElements`](https://maven.fabricmc.net/docs/fabric-api-0.155.2+26.1.2/net/fabricmc/fabric/api/client/rendering/v1/hud/VanillaHudElements.html) offer a comparable alternative to NeoForge's `RegisterGuiLayersEvent`, and would improve mod compatibility with mods like Farmer's Delight Refabricated that also need to render on the food bar.

Not sure how far back you support, but this API is available in 1.21.6+ versions of Fabric API.

issues.title: 1.21.11 Spear Lunge causes Saturation bug.
issues.body:
Bug: Saturation bar doesn't update visually after large exhaustion spikes (e.g. from combat mechanics that drain 3–5 saturation points at once)
Environment:

AppleSkin version: appleskin-fabric-mc1.21.11-3.0.8.jar
Minecraft: 1.21.11 Fabric
No mod conflicts
Only change: saturation color overridden via resource pack

Steps to reproduce:

Be at full saturation (any level works though)
Perform a spear lunge (really only affects spearmace kit pvp) repeatedly

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lh5R3Vudl_s (this is a montage, and I'm sorry for the red color which probably causes issues to see clearly)
0:04, 0:10, 0:26 (depicts is fixing itself when sat bar reaches 0), 0:38. There are many more instances throughout the video.

0:07 shows that only the saturation bar is bugged, vanilla hunger bar is correct

Expected: Saturation overlay updates to reflect the new lower saturation level
Actual: Saturation bar stays visually "full" (ghost bar) (or at the level at which you spear lunge) — doesn't refresh until you eat food or fully deplete saturation. Similar to ghost blocks — placing a block near one refreshes it; same concept here, any food interaction fixes the display temporarily.
Likely cause: The HUD overlay renders a stale/cached saturation value when the drop is sudden and large (multiple points lost in a single tick). Normal regen drains saturation 1 point at a time so it never triggers this.

I wanted to make a new addon mod, but it would be difficult for both of us so I decided to mention it here.

Config screen doesn’t open without Cloth Config installed
issues.body:
When using Mod Menu, the "Configure" button is visible for this mod.
However, clicking it does nothing if Cloth Config is not installed.

The mod appears to use Cloth Config for its config screen, but
cloth-config is not declared as a dependency in fabric.mod.json.

Because of this:
- Fabric does not warn the user
- Mod Menu still shows the Configure button
- The config screen silently fails to open

Suggested fix:
Add cloth-config as a required dependency, or conditionally
register the config screen only when Cloth Config is present.

issues.body:
AppleSkin doesn't hide correctly with [AutoHUD](https://modrinth.com/mod/autohud) on Neoforge 1.21.1, while on Fabric it renders perfectly fine.

# Forge
Minecraft Version: 1.21.1
NeoForge Version: 21.1.128
Mods:
- [AppleSkin](https://modrinth.com/mod/EsAfCjCV) [3\.0\.5\+mc1\.21] by squeek (appleskin\-neoforge\-mc1\.21\-3\.0\.5\.jar)
- [Auto HUD](https://modrinth.com/mod/temczoTQ) [8\.2] by Crendgrim (autohud\-8\.2\+1\.21\.1\-neoforge\.jar)

AppleSkin related elements don't move with the hud

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95263f27-cbf5-4a34-9240-6ba316972bf1)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/286bb13a-0b5e-48f3-93d6-7638a28b9f23)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d7f663a-dfb1-44f7-afe4-67e03db6300c)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c570af18-5eff-4fe5-9d80-9401258daf4b)

# Fabric
Minecraft Version: 1.21.1
Fabric Version: 0.16.10
Mods: 
- [AppleSkin](https://modrinth.com/mod/EsAfCjCV) [3\.0\.6\+mc1\.21] by squeek502 (appleskin\-fabric\-mc1\.21\-3\.0\.6\.jar)
- [Auto HUD](https://modrinth.com/mod/temczoTQ) [8\.2] by Crendgrim (autohud\-8\.2\+1\.21\.1\-fabric\.jar)
- [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/P7dR8mSH) [0\.115\.1\+1\.21\.1] by FabricMC (fabric\-api\-0\.115\.1\+1\.21\.1\.jar)

Works perfectly.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27b73493-edbb-414a-bed8-3919657b3848)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89ea341d-679f-44f3-96ff-1e4b8c0ff411)

# Sinytra Connector 

It seems that if I use the Fabric version of AppleSkin (via [Sinytra Connector](https://modrinth.com/mod/connector) on NeoForge) , with the NeoForge version of AutoHUD (the fabric version of AutoHUD crashes), then it does work! So **it seems to be an issue with AppleSkin's Neoforge version.**

Mods used on Sinytra Connector:
- [AppleSkin](https://modrinth.com/mod/EsAfCjCV) [3\.0\.6\+mc1\.21] by squeek502 (appleskin\-fabric\-mc1\.21\-3\.0\.6\.jar)
- [Auto HUD](https://modrinth.com/mod/temczoTQ) [8\.2] by Crendgrim (autohud\-8\.2\+1\.21\.1\-neoforge\.jar)
- [Forgified Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/Aqlf1Shp) [0\.107\.0\+2\.0\.23\+1\.21\.1] by Sinytra, FabricMC (forgified\-fabric\-api\-0\.107\.0\+2\.0\.23\+1\.21\.1\.jar)
- [Sinytra Connector](https://modrinth.com/mod/u58R1TMW) [mk9pRgwU] (connector\-2\.0\.0\-beta\.7\+1\.21\.1\-full\.jar)

Hi,
 
I'm reaching out because I'd like to integrate my mod with yours. My mod adds attributes for maximum hunger and saturation, and I'd like to explore ways to display these values correctly using your mod's interface.
 
Specifically, I'm wondering if it's possible for your mod to retrieve the maximum hunger and saturation values from my mod. Additionally, I'd be interested in exploring the implementation of a stacking feature for the saturation bar, allowing it to overlap with my mod's hunger bar.
 
Would you be open to discussing this integration further?
 
Thank you for your time and consideration.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8b9df34-0bf8-4e2b-bd32-4cec23b41ae2)
Render non-scaled text but offset saturation line 1-pixel lower.

issues.title: Investigate adding support for Configured for Fabric mod config menu
issues.body:
Currently the Fabric version of AppleSkin uses autoconfig + clothconfig for its config file and mod menu config screen integration. This works fine, but it means that AppleSkin includes a copy of Cloth as a jar-in-jar, which accounts for most of the size of the AppleSkin jar (1.1MiB jar with cloth, 76.7KiB without it).

[Configured](https://github.com/MrCrayfish/Configured), instead, works more like ModMenu, where it automatically generates mod config screens for supported configs and is installed separately. For the NeoForge/Forge versions of AppleSkin, Configured works out-of-the-box.

However, to use Configured on Fabric, AFAICT AppleSkin would need to either:
- Use a supported config system; it lists [Framework](https://github.com/MrCrayfish/Framework) or JEI
  + Not a fan of this option, as it'd mean taking on a (different) dependency that we'd likely have to include in the AppleSkin jar
- Use the [Configured API](https://github.com/MrCrayfish/Configured/tree/multiloader/1.20.6/common/src/main/java/com/mrcrayfish/configured/api) to provide config information
  + This should mean that we only need to build against the Configured API with no runtime dependency

Just something to consider.

Other notes:
- Would also want to make sure any existing config files can be transferred over to the new system transparently
- Would want to make sure the [localizations](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin/blob/1.20.5-fabric/resources/assets/appleskin/lang/en_us.json) can be used with Configured

issues.title: Compatibility Issue with Sinytra Connector, Forge, and AppleSkin
issues.body:
I'm experiencing a compatibility problem with the Sinytra Connector, Forge, and AppleSkin combination while running Spice of Fabric on Forge. It appears that AppleSkin isn't functioning properly in this setup. With the Forge version, I can access the main screen, but end up crashing when attempting to enter a world. Moreover, the Fabric version fails to load altogether.

While the mod itself works fine with Spice of Fabric, it only operates properly when the loader is Fabric. It would be beneficial to resolve this issue to enable the diminishing systems of Spice of Fabric in Forge with the Sinytra Connector, as AppleSkin currently causes crashes in both Forge and Fabric versions with the Forge loader.

issues.title: No option to disable Bedrockify screen safe area compat when the related mixin is disabled
issues.body:
I'm using another mod (Overflowing Bars) which does not support Bedrockify moving the hotbar, so I use Raised mod to move it up and disable the screen safe area mixin from Bedrockify (client.features.screenSafeArea). This sets the hotbar back at it's normal position and instead relies on Raised mod to move the hotbar. Now, I set the screen safe area back to 15 so it affects only Bedrockify widgets.
See that the effect to Bedrockify widgets remains without the mixin:
![image](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin/assets/160344941/8e6a4bb1-5fc5-4a68-af18-8047ea4bfac6)
^ (0 screen safe area)

![image](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin/assets/160344941/fa502ffb-0051-4980-b021-6d53b7c87c60)
^ (15 screen safe area)

I prefer to have it at 15 because 0 is right at the screen corner. But AppleSkin mod apparently reads the Bedrockify screen safe area, regardless of the hotbar effects being enabled, and mistakenly places the saturation at where it might be if the hotbar was moved there.
![image](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin/assets/160344941/6d6ef948-4a53-46af-a9f1-429c9ea3f542)
^ (Mixin disabled, screen safe area 15)

Preferred fix might be to add an option to disable the Bedrockify compatibility and/or intelligently disable it when the mixin is not enabled for the hotbar effects.

Raised mod properly affects the Overflowing Bars widgets, this compatibility is not the focus of this issue.
Bedrockify mod does not affect the Overflowing Bars widgets, which is the reason I need this compatibility.

issues.title: Health overlay rendering while frozen from powder snow
issues.body:
Like the title says, while frozen from being in powder snow the heart icons being rendered while holding food are normal hearts.

To reproduce: place down powder snow using a bucket, walk into it and hold a food item. This results in:
![javaw_20240318-144626-958_(Minecraft_1 20 2_-_Multiplayer_(LAN))](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin/assets/8273440/515dc3d9-3f28-4f0f-9fc6-86921cf0d2cd)

The rendering should probably be disabled the same way it is when affected by poison or wither effects. For this there is a `isFullyFrozen()` method inside the `Player` class.

I am unsure how early Mojang implemented those custom heart icons while freezing, but I have tested this with 1.20.2 and above.

issues.title: [API] Allow for specifying whether an item can be consumed or not
issues.body:
MC: 1.20.2
Loader: Fabric
AppleSkin Version: 2.5.1

Currently, in Origins Fabric, we use custom logic in the edible item power type to allow for any item to become edible if an entity is given a specific type of power.
We are unable to use Fabric's built-in API for this as it is more of a compile time thing for specific items, rather than a general use allowed on every item thing.

The issue is that we are unable to specify whether an item can be consumed or not through the API. So items that aren't usually consumable will never show their hunger/saturation in AppleSkin.

This would also be very useful for cases where an item shouldn't be consumable too, such as for the prevent item use power type.

issues.title: question regarding package private classes
issues.body:
Hi, this is a bit of a weird request and I totally understand if you don't feel like doing it.
I am trying to develop a mod, which would allow the hunger bar icons to be overridden per player depending on specific conditions.
It would be really nice to have support for AppleSkin, but in order for me to accomplish that, I would have to mixin to some of it's classes, which right now is a bit difficult, because some inner classes it uses during the rendering process are package-private.

I guess there is no actual reason for them to be non-public, other than them not being useful to anyone simply using the API, but it would make things a lot easier for me if they were. The affected classes are `TooltipOverlayHandler$FoodTooltipRenderer`, `TooltipOverlayHandler$TextureOffsets` and `HudOverlayHandler$RenderOverlayType`.

issues.title: Consider using mod_version instead of combined version for fabric jars
issues.body:
Whenever I load up appleskin via fabric, I get this warning:

```
[21:00:09] [main/WARN]: Mod `appleskin` (mc1.17.1-2.2.0) does not respect SemVer - comparison support is limited.
```

Ideally, the `fabric.mod.json` should be modified to use something semver compatible, which means either replacing `"version": "${version}"` with `"version": "${mod_version}"` or providing a "flipped" version string for Fabric like `2.2.0-mc1.17.1`.

Personally, I would use `${mod_version}` as the version string and additionally constrain the Minecraft version directly in the Fabric dependencies, adding: `"minecraft": ">=${minecraft_version}"` to the `"depends"` map.

Am willing to help provide specific PRs for this, but not sure what branches would be appropriate to send to, since the forge and fabric code is kept in separate branches, and I'm not sure what's maintained.

issues.title: Release on modrinth.com
issues.body:
Modrinth is an alternative to curseforge which is way better in a few key aspects:
  -  Proper filtering
     - on curseforge you can search for 1.17 mods, or fabric mods, not 1.17 fabric mods
     - it also has client/server mod filters
  -  Fast searches
     -  It takes nanoseconds for the search results to update to what you have typed, as opposed to the 3-5 seconds curseforge does
  - Easier API integration
     - Well documented, easy to use api
     - You can ask for support from actual humans

Along with this, there are a bunch of people who would like to use your mod, but won't go to curseforge to get it.

issues.title: Crashes with the combo of mods I use - 1.16.4
Feature Request: off-hand food hunger preview changes
issues.body:
I always run around with a baked potato in my off-hand.

The UI showing these *empty* hunger elements as *visually* not-exactly-empty over 50% of the time (including fading in/out) is very distracting and confusing to have engaged permanently. (However, the preview is certainly too useful to pass up entirely.)

I was wondering if any of the following could be implemented as an option **for food in the off-hand**:

* Disabling it entirely: only food in the main hand has its hunger previewed
* Reduce it: e.g. blinking only every *other* time
* Discretize it: remove the fade-in and fade-out animation

Thanks,  
-- James

[ModUpdater](https://gitea.thebrokenrail.com/TheBrokenRail/ModUpdater) is a Fabric mod that checks for and downloads updates to cooperating Fabric mods.

There are [a couple ways](https://gitea.thebrokenrail.com/TheBrokenRail/ModUpdater/src/branch/master/MOD_DEVELOPER.md) to support ModUpdater, but none of them are *quite* straightforward here; it looks like you would either need to change the Jar file naming convention to put the AppleSkin version before the Minecraft version, or host and update a JSON file for which AppleSkin version you need for each minecraft version.

issues.title: Exhaustion bar is copied with very high exhaustion levels (200+)
issues.body:
As of AppleCore 3.4.0 for MC 1.12.2 plus AppleSkin 1.0.9, with a high enough exhaustion cap, it is possible to get the exhaustion bar to copy itself multiple times, like so:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37945304/83929659-cc50d980-a759-11ea-80bb-5472f742d035.png)

To reproduce:
1. Install the aforementioned mods. For easier reproduction, also install Scaling Feast 1.5.0 by @yeelp, which sets the exhaustion cap to `Float.MAX_VALUE`.
2. In the configs for Scaling Feast, set `food cap` -> `Hunger Damage Multiplier` to a value higher than 0.
3. If you have set `Hunger Damage Multiplier` to 1.0, then do `/gamerule mobGriefing false` (recommended) and then `/summon creeper ~ ~ ~ {Fuse:0,ExplosionRadius:127}`. This will cause you to take ~2,600 HP of damage, gaining over 10,000 exhaustion points in the process.
4. If you have set `Hunger Damage Multiplier` to 1000.0, then find or summon a hostile mob and let it attack you. This will also cause you to gain thousands of exhaustion points.
5. Take a look at the exhaustion bar.

issues.title: [1.12.2, Bug] Graphical glitch with high exhaustion values.
issues.body:
When a player has a really high exhaustion value that exceeds their max exhaustion, AppleSkin draws the following graphical glitch to the bottom left of the screen.
![exhaustbad](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22644157/83676881-5c035600-a5a9-11ea-88f3-3453cce891bb.png)

This can occur in vanilla even with the maximum exhaustion value being capped at 40. However, with AppleCore now being able to change this exhaustion cap as of version 3.4.0, this graphical bug will probably occur more frequently as modders experiment with it.

The solution as far as I see is to clamp the ```ratio``` float right here https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin/blob/ef2b13167424de3958e54344155315dbf99f0908/java/squeek/appleskin/client/HUDOverlayHandler.java#L188 to never be greater than 1 (unless there's a specific reason it's unbounded), as I presume the texture just wraps around if the length of the texture exceeds the length of the texture map.

I haven't checked the other branches for the different AppleSkin versions, but I imagine this occurs in all the other versions. I can double check and open a PR patching this for 1.12.2. I'm embarrassed to say my knowledge with Git isn't as expansive as I'd like it to be, so I don't know if it's possible to open a PR that will patch all branches simultaneously (I suspect not).

issues.title: [1.12.2] Modified vanilla fish items not displaying correctly
issues.body:
AppleSkin isn't reflecting the changes to the foodValue / saturationModifier for any of the `<minecraft:fish:*>` or `<minecraft:cooked_fish:*>`.

(Note: strictly for Minecraft 1.12, before the vanilla fish items were split into separate IDs)

I've been testing Mrbysco's latest update to FoodTweaker, which added support for modifying food items with metadata (such as fish / golden apple variants).
I'm using a simple test script for FoodTweaker which modifies a list of vanilla foods to give maximum food and saturation values so that I can quickly confirm that changes have been applied correctly.
(see the script here for more info: https://paste.dimdev.org/raruxadogi.xml)

As demonstrated in this screenshot, it's working as intended for most foods, including those with metadata such as the 'enchanted' golden apple:
![2020-03-11_11 03 57](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3400211/76363593-3ab71300-6388-11ea-84ab-e7e4a58216c8.png)

However, it's not displaying the updated information for the any of the 4x minecraft:fish or the 2x minecraft:cooked_fish:
![2020-03-11_10 53 04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3400211/76363812-adc08980-6388-11ea-813a-0c3c30519775.png)
...Even though eating one does indeed restore my hunger bar to full, as demonstrated in the comparison with the next screenshot:
![2020-03-11_10 58 13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3400211/76363909-ea8c8080-6388-11ea-8c5a-8edee64caad9.png)

~

Versions:
* Minecraft 1.12.2
* Forge 14.23.5.2847
* AppleSkin-mc1.12-1.0.9
* CraftTweaker2-1.12-4.1.20
* FoodTweaker-1.1.1

Original issue on FoodTweaker's side: https://github.com/Mrbysco/FoodTweaker/issues/2

issues.title: Suggestion: Style Config Option
issues.body:
This mod is such a boon to quality of life; I can't begin to say just how useful it is.
One thing has always bothered me a bit though: The appearance of the tooltip.
Rather than seamlessly integrating into the tooltip, it instead adds a grey box on the bottom. In comparison to mods that do similar things (Quark's Food Tooltip [which doesn't show saturation], Quark's Stat Display, the Tough As Nails AppleSkin addon) put the icons inside the tooltip of the item.

I know it's not a major issue, but as a person who has a very particular aesthetic sense and who likes things to fit in, I would really appreciate a config option at least to change the display to be more in-line with other such mods and fit in with the tooltips better in general.

I've included the Quark Food Tooltip image, and the AppleSkin Tough As Nails addon Hydration Tooltip image as reference for what I mean.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40530630/45883888-30a1ee80-bd67-11e8-8fae-23b534a045cc.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40530630/45883908-40b9ce00-bd67-11e8-993b-36559df0d5f1.png)

I've been testing this with a mod pack, which can be found [here](http://www.modlister.com/user/XvSkItZvX), noticed that thirst mechanic, from the "Tough as Nails" mod behaves as though there is some sort of saturation(hydration) mechanic. issues.title: Food tooltip is not working if NEI is installed
issues.body:
When NEI is installed, food tooltip is not showing up when looking at the item inside the inventory.
It also doesn't work when NEI item panel and NEI recipe searcher are used, but works fine with those from JEI.

This was already reported to NEI bug tracker back in August and in December by two other guys, but there was no response.
I'm reporting it here hoping that the fix is possible from this end.

Versions:
Forge 12.18.3.2185
CodeChickenCore 2.4.0.100
CodeChickenLib 2.5.1.185
NotEnoughItems 2.1.3.182
JEI 3.14.2.401
AppleSkin 1.0.5
